create.name: Eric Zimmer
create.bio:
Eric Zimmer is an American behaviour coach, certified interfaith spiritual director and Zen student, best known as the creator and host of The One You Feed. The podcast takes its name from the old story of two wolves struggling inside each of us, and across more than a decade and some 900 episodes he has used it to talk with writers, scientists and meditation teachers about how people really change. His own turning point came after a very hard stretch in his twenties, including a time without a home, and the practices that carried him through became the core of what he now teaches. Before coaching full time he worked in software and large project management, and founded a solar energy company that trained returning veterans.

His approach pairs behavioural science with contemplative wisdom and keeps the steps small: notice what the mind is pulling towards, choose one modest action, and repeat it. He works with clients one to one in a six-month coaching programme, runs a short email course on finding calm in the middle of a busy day, and gives talks and workshops to companies and nonprofits. His first book, How a Little Becomes a Lot (HarperCollins, 2026), sets out this way of making lasting change. He lives in Atlanta.

books.title: How a Little Becomes a Lot: The Art of Small Changes for a More Meaningful Life
books.author: Eric Zimmer
books.description: Zimmer's first book, published by HarperCollins in March 2026. It argues that change lasts when we stop forcing ourselves and instead work patiently with the competing pulls of the mind, one small choice at a time, drawing on behavioural research and contemplative teaching.

courses.title: The Aligned Progress Method: 1:1 Coaching with Eric Zimmer
courses.description: A six-month one-to-one coaching programme with Eric, starting with two sessions a month and moving to monthly calls, supported by a simple framework and weekly check-ins. Places are limited and you apply for a spot.

courses.title: Overwhelm is Optional
courses.description: A four-week course delivered by email, about ten minutes a day. It teaches short ways to reset your attention during an ordinary busy day, using the moments between tasks rather than extra time on the cushion.

courses.title: The One You Feed Membership on Patreon
courses.description: Listener membership for the podcast, with a free tier and a paid tier for supporters. Members back the show and get extra material from Eric and the team.

free_resources.title: The One You Feed podcast
free_resources.description: Eric's weekly show, now past 900 episodes, in which he talks with authors, researchers and meditation teachers about living with more wisdom and purpose. Every episode is free to stream.

free_resources.title: Eric Zimmer on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: A free collection of long-form conversations from the podcast, including talks with Tara Brach, Adyashanti and Dan Siegel. Free to listen in the app or on the web.

free_resources.title: Free Masterclass: Habits That Stick
free_resources.description: A free recorded webinar on staying consistent with a new habit, covering how to set goals that keep you going and the pillars Eric uses with coaching clients. Watch straight away after signing up.

free_resources.title: How to Quiet Your Inner Critic
free_resources.description: A free three-part mindfulness training on noticing the harsh inner voice, working with it rather than fighting it, and easing the habit of comparing yourself with others.

free_resources.title: Free guide: How to Stick to a Meditation Practice
free_resources.description: A short downloadable guide to the five common mistakes that make people give up on meditation, with Eric's suggestions for building a practice that lasts.

flags: Health rule, unsure so plan written: his own offerings (coaching, email course, membership, free trainings) are not sold on conditions, but oneyoufeed.net's main menu lists podcast categories 'Anxiety & Depression' and 'Addiction & Recovery', he pitches talks to 'patient communities', and his story of recovering from heroin addiction is central to his brand pages; owner to decide whether that counts as a brand sold on conditions.
Instagram, Facebook and YouTube are the podcast's brand accounts (Instagram carries his name); counted because the brand is his own show, but the tier is local_hero either way.
A possible editorial-stature case (HarperCollins author, long-running podcast with a large audience) was not applied; owner may want to consider luminary.
No personal email published; the contact page asks guests to write to a guest-requests inbox (obfuscated in text), which was not used; general contact is the form.
Partner Ginny Gay is listed on the site as co-host/team; not a separate listing.
All videos are on other channels (TEDx, interviews where he is the main speaker); his own channel holds podcast interviews with guests, which were left out.
Insight Timer bio could not be saved word for word (WebFetch would only quote the opening line and phrases); the bio check used that partial text plus his own pages.
left_out: Habits That Matter group programme (offers.oneyoufeed.net/wisehabits/): the page currently shows a template placeholder (polar bear fundraiser, lorem ipsum), so it could not be verified.
Transformation Program (ericzimmer.coach) and Spiritual Habits Workshop (thespiritualhabit.com): domains did not respond.
Podcast episodes and videos with condition-named titles (anxiety, depression, addiction, trauma, chronic illness, memory loss) left out under the health rule.
Insight Timer tracks not listed individually; no Insight Timer courses found.
Instagram @ericzimmer (11 followers) not linked or counted: not clearly his.
TED talk link oneyoufeed.net/ted resolves to the TEDxColumbus video, included as a video.
No in-person base for classes or sessions (lives in Atlanta, coaches online), so availability is worldwide.
